CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  January 23, 2025-2:00 P.M.  I

  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING

 Pursuant to Resolution No. 10110, the City Council Meeting was held and convened remotely
  via videoconference/teleconference in compliance with the Brown Act.
OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 2:02 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Hampton. (Absent:
  None)

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Councilmember Rick Cole
  CouncilmemberTyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney Michele Beat Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO SUSPEND THE COLLECTION OF
  PARKING FEES FOR PREFERENTIAL PARKING GUEST
  PASSES, OVERNIGHT PARKING PERMITS AND PARKING IN
  CITY GARAGE FACILITIES, FOR VEHICLES REGISTERED AT
  ADDRESSES DAMAGED OR DESTROYED IN THE EATON FIRE
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  "project" subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and
  within the meaning ofCEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b);
  (2) Adopt a resolution to suspend the collection of parking fees for
  (Resolution No. 10113):
  a. Up to three additional annual guest preferential parking
  permits per account address for vehicles that are registered
  to addresses that were damaged or destroyed in the Eaton
  Fire;
  b. Additional overnight parking permits, in excess of the limit of
  two, to residents hosting vehicles that are registered to
  addresses that were damaged or destroyed in the Eaton Fire,
  except
  c. Vehicles registered to addresses that were damaged or
  destroyed in the Eaton Fire to park in City parking facilities
  with available capacity for up to 30 days.

Council Minutes  1  01/23/2025
   Joaquin Siques, Director of Transportation, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the item, and responded to questions.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Hampton, seconded by
  Councilmember Cole, to approve the staff recommendation.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Jones, Lyon,
  Madison, Masuda, Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  UPDATE - CITY RESPONSE TO WINDSTORMS AND FIRES -
  CITY MANAGER AND EMERGENCY OPERATIONS STAFF
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Consider updates from City staff and provide direction if desired
  by the City Council; and
  (2) Find that, if direction is given to staff, it would not be a "project"
  subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and within the
  meaning ofCEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b).

  Chad Augustin, Fire Chief, provided a status update on the Eaton
  fire containment, the remaining areas under Do-Not-Drink water
  advisory, the forecasted rain for the upcoming weekend, and the
  City's preparations for mud and debris flow, and responded to
  questions.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding k-rails and
  mud flow preparations, Greg de Vinck, Public Works Director,
  reported that City crews are on standby to place k-rails if needed,
  and the City does have an operational contract with a k-rail vendor
  who is also on standby if additional assistance is required.

  In response to comments by Councilmember Jones advocating for
  Pasadena Water and Power to assess and consider acquiring
  Altadena's water utilities, David Reyes, Acting General Manager of
  Water and Power, reported that City staff is in contact with local
  water agencies that serve Altadena and is offering assistance and
  support through the City's water leases and interconnection
  agreements but noted that no further discussions have occurred.
  City Attorney Bagneris and Acting General Manager Reyes stated
  that such actions would require extensive legal research and would
  need to be initiated by those independent agencies.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for the City to assist employees who
  lost their homes with navigating through the process of rebuilding in
  addition to proving other support and resources.

Council Minutes  2  01/23/2025
   Manuel Carmona, Acting Director of Public Health, reported on air
  quality and soil testing options. He reported on potential gaps of
  Mayor Gordo left the  tracking air quality and fluctuating particulate matter. He stated that
  meeting at 2:07 p.m. to  the City will continue to have discussions with the Environmental
  attend multi-agency  Protection Agency (EPA), FEMA, AQMD, and regional partners to
  meeting that conflicted  develop an approach addressing air quality and soil testing.
  with this Council meeting.
  Paul Wennburg, Caltech Professor, presented information on air
  quality and particulate matter, and responded to questions.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding testing and
  clean up of the City's pools and playgrounds, Koko Panossian,
  Parks, Recreation and Community Services Director, reported that
  the pools were thoroughly cleaned, passing all sanitation
  requirements, and added that City staff is sanitizing all playgrounds
  and will remove and replace 3 inches of sand from all play areas.

  Discussion ensued regarding how residents can safely clean their
  homes, the importance of wearing protective and effective masks,
  the correlation between air quality and direction of air flow, and low-
  cost air quality sensors and purifiers.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry regarding the
  hazardous materials removal process, Bill Jones, EPA
  representative, reported that EPA officers will be working in teams to
  collect hazmat waste (i.e., paint cans, car batteries, etc.) from burnt
L
  sites and transport them to a staging site in Irwindale. Israel Del Toro,
  Planning Deputy Director, also reported that during Phase 2 of the
  debris cleanup process, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will
  remove and transport damaged vehicles to a staging site for
  adjudication.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one tetter expressing concerns with
  the City's response to the Eaton Fire and the City's relationship with
  a local nonprofit, one letter advocating for the City Council to prohibit
  rent increases during the City's State of Emergency, and one letter
  expressing concerns with the City's lack of information related to the
  fire, were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City
  Council, posted online, and made part of the public record for the
  item.

  John Butler, Pasadena resident, inquired when the City would
  be picking up green waste from sidewalks.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Vice Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.
